root: ^bewildered her. Swinging blades like pendulums hissed through the corridor, eager to slice.
^But she was fierce. Agile. In one fluid sweep of a whirlwind dance, Alice rolled forward like wind through reeds.
^The blades never even saw her coming.
^Now just steps away from the treasure chest—rumored to contain riches beyond imagination—she halted. The floor ahead didn’t feel right.
^False ground, ready to collapse beneath her feet.
^But Alice, ever the cat, stepped back just in time. The stone cracked where she would’ve stood.
^You might think it obvious. But when a moment is all you have, when death is just one blink away, reacting like that takes cold blood... and a quicker mind.
^Her quest was nearly over. She could almost taste victory.
^A skeleton rose, bones creaking, eye sockets hollow—but full of menace.
^“Fine. One more nuisance,” she muttered, pulling her twin daggers with a flick, pointedly ignoring her sledgehammer.
^“Too much ado about nothing,” she said under her breath.
^Truth be told, the fight took longer than expected. She danced around the creature—rolling forward, then back—evading each bone-crushing swing.
^“Too tough, huh?” she sighed, and in one swift motion, her dagger vanished—replaced with a hammer so massive, it looked like overkill carved into steel.
^ “Bone dust,” she snorted. “Maybe some alchemist'll trade for it... if I can scoop it up without sneezing.”
^ But before she could even bend down, more coffins groaned. More skeletons emerged—angrier this time.
^ “More bone walkers,” she grumbled. “They must’ve died cursed to be this clingy after death.”
^She was confident, yes—but the hammer slowed her. Multiple enemies closed in. She hesitated.
^When it seemed she might be overwhelmed, she twirled. A full whirlwind. The hammer swept through the boneyards—shattering skeletons like porcelain.
^“Alright,” she exhaled. “That must be the last of them.”
^She stepped up to the chest and opened it.
^The silence didn’t last. The ground shook. A far coffin shattered.
^From it emerged the biggest skeleton of them all—armor still clinging to his corpse, his eyes burning with undead fury.
^“No time for this. I’m tired. There’s no bonfire in sight. And I just got cheated by an empty chest.”
^She raised her hammer. “Come here, skelli. You’d better be holding something worthwhile.”
^She used every trick she had—dodging, parrying, even draining her mana for enchanted strikes. When she ran dry, she chugged a healing and magic potions like a champ.
^This one was tougher. But nothing outlasts a hammer brazed in flames. And a deadly heavy attack!
^Alice lit the weapon with fire and brought it down like divine judgment.
^Bones scattered. The skeleton lord was no more.
^“A boss token...” she muttered, picking it up. “Great. Useless. Unless I find a blacksmith. Maybe he can forge it into a spell... or a weapon…”
^“All I care about is gold anyway.”
^“Wait... Boss token… I can just consume it for gold.”
^Her pouch bulged, gold spilling between her fingers as she counted, grinning ear to ear.
^So distracted was she by her newfound wealth, she forgot the swinging blades that had nearly claimed her once before.
^A clean slice — and she was ham in an instant.
^Next thing she knew, she was back at the last bonfire.
^“No…” she groaned, slumping. “I lost all my gold... and now I have to go back through that damn cavern...”
^She looked up at the night sky, exasperated.
^“One of these days, gold will definitely be the end of me.”
